definitions.explanation: a person who performs acrobatics, juggling, or other feats of physical skill

examples.japanese: サーカスの{曲芸師|きょくげいし}がすごい{技|わざ}を{見|み}せた。
examples.english: The circus acrobat showed an amazing trick.

examples.japanese: {曲芸師|きょくげいし}が{綱|つな}の{上|うえ}で{自転車|じてんしゃ}に{乗|の}っている。
examples.english: The acrobat is riding a bicycle on a tightrope.

examples.japanese: {幼|おさな}いころからサーカスで{育|そだ}った{彼女|かのじょ}は、{一流|いちりゅう}の{曲芸師|きょくげいし}として{世界中|せかいじゅう}を{回|まわ}っている。
examples.english: Having grown up in the circus since childhood, she travels the world as a top-class acrobat.

notes:
Composed of {曲芸|きょくげい} (acrobatics/tricks) and {師|し} (master/professional). Refers to professional performers of acrobatic feats, juggling, and similar physical skills. While associated with circuses, traditional Japanese {曲芸|きょくげい} also includes street performance traditions dating back centuries.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- サーカスの{曲芸師|きょくげいし}: circus acrobat
- {大道|だいどう}{曲芸師|きょくげいし}: street performer
- {曲芸師|きょくげいし}の{技|わざ}: acrobat's trick

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {曲芸|きょくげい}: acrobatics — the art itself rather than the performer
- {大道芸人|だいどうげいにん}: street performer — broader term for any street entertainer
- {軽業師|かるわざし}: acrobat — older, more literary term emphasizing lightness and agility
- ジャグラー: juggler — specifically someone who juggles
